sentences.text: Xinminosaurus was a reptile belonging to the cymbospondylid ichthyosaurs that lived during the Middle Triassic in Guizhou Province, China.
Its name combines the district of Xinmin where it was found with the Greek word for lizard, while the species name means "crusher" due to its unique bulbous, laterally compressed teeth.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — measured 2.32 meters in total length and possessed a skull 29 centimeters long with 140 vertebrae.
The animal's teeth were bulbous and narrow from side to side, lacking constrictions in the back of the jaws, and the tips of the jaws may have been toothless while the front teeth were cone-shaped.
Replacement teeth were arranged in a second row rather than being located in pulp cavities.
The animal possessed unique bulbous, laterally compressed teeth specifically adapted for crushing.
The tail bent downwards at a 35-degree angle starting at the 38th caudal vertebra.
The foreflipper digits contained a small number of bones compared to other ichthyosaurs, with counts of 3, 5, 5, 5, and 2.
The species is known only from a nearly complete holotype skeleton housed at the Geological Museum of Peking University, discovered near Yangjuan Village in the Xinmin District of Panxian County.
The fossils were found in the upper member of the Guanling Formation within the Nicoraella kockeli biozone.
Approximately 60 vertebrae were located in front of the hips, a high number similar to other ichthyosaurs.
The limb bones of Xinminosaurus were atypical for an ichthyosaur, with the upper arm bones featuring bladelike projections on their front edges, a characteristic of ichthyopterygians.
Xinminosaurus is classified within the parent group Omphalosauridae, and the family of Xinminosaurus is Omphalosauridae.

Researchers have debated whether Xinminosaurus is a valid genus or merely a junior synonym of Tholodus, with Maisch arguing that the main difference between the two is size, with Tholodus being twice as large.
Mulder and Jagt (2019) suggested that the teeth of the mosasaur Globidens timorensis resemble those of the ichthyosaurs Tholodus and Xinminosaurus.
